Emperor penguins, the world's largest penguin species, to decline by 26-47% by 2050 if global climate warming continues. The emperor penguin is the largest of his 18 species of penguins inhabiting the world, growing to about 120 centimeters in length and about 40 kilograms in weight. Species with a global population of over 500,000 are easier to hunt due to worsening global heat budgets, greenhouse gas and carbon emissions, and declining sea ice. At the same time, these penguins have difficulty finding food and the widespread impacts of climate change have severely hampered their chances of survival. (Photo by Sebnem Coskun/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images)
